title_en: Opinion of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the Ministry of Public Security, and the Ministry of Justice on Severely Punishing Crimes of Sexual Assault Against Minors According to Law

articles.content_en:
I. Basic Requirements
1. The crimes of sexual assault against minors as referred to in this Opinion include the crimes of rape against minors, forcible indecency and insult against women, child molestation, organizing prostitution, forcing prostitution, luring, harboring, and introducing prostitution, luring underage girls into prostitution, and patronizing underage prostitutes as provided for in Articles 236, 237, 358, 359, and paragraph 2 of Article 360 of the Criminal Law.
2. Crimes of sexual assault against minors shall be severely punished according to law.
3. When handling cases of sexual assault against minors, full consideration shall be given to the characteristics of minor victims, such as their incomplete physical and mental development and vulnerability to harm, and the principle of special and priority protection shall be implemented to effectively safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of minors.
4. Where a minor commits a crime of sexual assault against another minor, the principle of dual protection shall be adhered to. While protecting the legitimate rights and interests of the minor victim according to law, the legitimate rights and interests of the minor criminal suspect and the minor defendant shall also be protected according to law.
5. When handling cases of sexual assault against minors, with respect to the identity information of the minor victim, minor criminal suspect, and minor defendant, as well as materials from which their identity information may be inferred, and details concerning the sexual assault, judicial personnel, procuratorial personnel, investigative personnel, lawyers, and other litigation participants shall maintain confidentiality.
Litigation documents disclosed to the public shall not disclose the identity information of the minor victim or other materials from which their identity information may be inferred, and the facts of the sexual assault shall be described in an appropriate manner.
6. Cases of sexual assault against minors shall be handled by judicial personnel, procuratorial personnel, and investigative personnel who are familiar with the physical and mental characteristics of minors. If the minor victim is female, female staff members shall participate.
If the People's Court, People's Procuratorate, or public security organ has a special institution or special working group for handling juvenile criminal cases, the special institution or special working group may give priority to handling cases of sexual assault against minors.
7. People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, public security organs, and judicial administrative organs at all levels shall strengthen contacts and cooperation with civil affairs, education, women's federations, Communist Youth League, and other departments, as well as minor protection organizations, to jointly carry out the prevention of sexual assault against minors and the psychological comfort and counseling of minor victims, and to provide necessary assistance to them from the perspective of being conducive to the physical and mental health of minors.
8. Higher-level People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, public security organs, and judicial administrative organs shall strengthen guidance and professional training for lower-level organs. People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, public security organs, and judicial administrative organs at all levels shall enhance the judicial concept of giving special and priority protection to minors, improve the working mechanism, and raise the capability and level of case handling.

II. Procedural Requirements for Case Handling
9. A person with special duties of guardianship, education, training, rescue, care, or medical treatment over a minor (hereinafter referred to as a person with special duties), as well as other citizens and entities, upon discovering that a minor has been subjected to sexual assault, have the right and duty to report or file a complaint with the public security organ, the People's Procuratorate, or the People's Court.
10. Upon receiving a report, complaint, or accusation that a minor has been subjected to sexual assault, the public security organ shall promptly accept it and rapidly conduct a review. If, upon review, the conditions for filing a case are met, the public security organ shall immediately file the case and initiate an investigation.
If the public security organ discovers that a minor may have been subjected to sexual assault or receives relevant leads, regardless of whether the case falls within its own jurisdiction, it shall promptly take emergency measures such as stopping the illegal or criminal act, protecting the victim, and preserving the scene. When necessary, it shall notify the relevant departments to provide temporary placement and relief for the victim.
11. If the People's Procuratorate considers that the public security organ should have filed a case for investigation but failed to do so, or if the victim or his or her legal representative, or a person with special duties over the minor, raises an objection to the People's Procuratorate on this ground, the People's Procuratorate shall request the public security organ to explain the reasons for not filing the case. If the People's Procuratorate deems the reasons for not filing the case as untenable, it shall notify the public security organ to file the case, and the public security organ shall file the case upon receiving such notification.
12. When investigating a case of sexual assault against a minor, the public security organ shall, in accordance with legal procedures, promptly and comprehensively collect and fix evidence. This includes promptly inspecting the crime scene of sexual assault, conducting physical examinations on the minor victim and the criminal suspect, extracting biological samples such as bodily fluids, hair, and residues under the fingernails of the victim and the suspect, as well as traces such as fingerprints, footprints, and shoe prints, and items such as clothing and buttons; promptly extracting documentary evidence such as accommodation registration forms, and audio-visual materials such as on-site surveillance videos; and promptly collecting evidence such as the victim's statement, witness testimony, and the suspect's confession.
13. When investigators go to the school, workplace, or residence of a minor victim or his or her relatives, or a minor witness, to collect evidence, they shall refrain from driving police vehicles, wearing uniforms, or adopting other methods that may expose the victim's identity or affect the victim's reputation or privacy.
14. When questioning a minor victim, the judicial personnel, procuratorial personnel, investigative personnel, and lawyers shall adhere to the principle of not causing harm, and shall choose the minor's residence or other places where the minor feels psychologically safe to conduct the questioning, and shall notify the minor's legal representative to be present. If the legal representative cannot be notified, cannot be present, or is a suspect or defendant of sexual assault, other adult relatives of the minor victim, or representatives from the minor's school, the local grassroots organization, or the minor protection organization, among others, may be notified to be present, and the relevant circumstances shall be recorded.
When questioning a minor victim, consideration shall be given to his or her physical and mental characteristics, and a gentle approach shall be adopted. A comprehensive inquiry shall be conducted regarding the facts related to the sexual assault, with the principle of conducting the inquiry once to avoid repeated questioning as much as possible.
15. When handling cases of sexual assault against minors, the People's Court and the People's Procuratorate shall promptly inform the minor victim and his or her legal representative or close relative of the right to entrust a litigation agent, and inform them that if they have financial difficulties, they may apply for legal aid from a legal aid institution. For those who need to apply for legal aid, the court or procuratorate shall assist them in applying for it. The legal aid institution shall promptly appoint a lawyer familiar with the physical and mental characteristics of minors to provide legal assistance.
16. When handling cases of crimes of sexual assault against minors, the People's Court, the People's Procuratorate, and the public security organ shall, except where it might impede the handling of the case, promptly inform the victim and his or her legal representative of the case progress and outcome, and explain the relevant circumstances.
17. After setting the trial date for a case of sexual assault against a minor, the People's Court shall notify the minor victim and his or her legal representative of the time and place of the trial. The legal representative of the minor victim may accompany or represent the minor victim in participating in the court proceedings and state opinions, except where the legal representative is the defendant in the sexual assault crime.
18. When the People's Court holds a trial for a case of sexual assault against a minor, if it is truly necessary for the minor victim or witness to appear in court, protective measures shall be taken based on the circumstances of the case, such as not exposing the appearance or real voice. Where conditions permit, the minor's statement or testimony may be played via video or other means, and protective measures shall also be taken when playing the video.

III. Accurate Application of Law
19. Where a person knows or should know that the other party is a girl under the age of 14 and commits sexual assault such as rape, the actor shall be deemed to have "knowledge" that the other party is a girl under the age of 14.
Where the victim is under the age of 12 and the actor commits sexual assault such as rape, the actor shall be deemed to have "knowledge" that the other party is a girl under the age of 14.
Where the victim is between the ages of 12 and 14, and based on observations such as the victim's physical development, speech and behavior, clothing characteristics, and daily routine, the victim may be a girl under the age of 14, and the actor commits sexual assault such as rape, the actor shall be deemed to have "knowledge" that the other party is a girl under the age of 14.
20. Where a person lures a girl under the age of 14 into having sexual relations with him or her by means of money, property, or other inducements; or where a person knows or should know that a girl under the age of 14 is being forced by another person into prostitution and still has sexual relations with her, both shall be punished as the crime of rape.
21. Where a person with special duties over a girl under the age of 14 has sexual relations with her, the act shall be punished as the crime of rape.
Where a person with special duties over a female minor who has reached the age of 14 uses his or her advantageous position or the victim's isolated and helpless situation to force the minor victim into submission and has sexual relations with her, the act shall be convicted and punished as the crime of rape.
22. Where a person commits a crime of child molestation, causing minor injury or more serious consequences to the child, and the act also meets the provisions of Article 234 or Article 232 of the Criminal Law, constituting the crime of intentional injury or intentional homicide, the person shall be convicted and punished according to the provision that imposes a heavier penalty.
Where a person commits an indecent act against a male minor who has reached the age of 14, causing minor injury or more serious consequences to the victim, and the act meets the provisions of Article 234 or Article 232 of the Criminal Law, the person shall be convicted and punished as the crime of intentional injury or intentional homicide.
23. Where a person commits a crime of rape or indecency against a minor in a public place such as a campus, swimming pool, or children's playground, as long as there are multiple other persons present, regardless of whether the persons present actually see the act, the act may be determined as "in public" rape of a woman, forcible indecency or insult against a woman, or child molestation in accordance with paragraph 3 of Article 236 and Article 237 of the Criminal Law.
24. Where a person introduces or assists another person in raping a girl under the age of 14 or molesting a child, the person shall be punished as an accomplice to the crime of rape or child molestation.
25. Where a person commits a crime of rape or indecency against a minor, the person shall be given a heavier punishment. In any of the following circumstances, the person shall be subject to severe punishment according to law:
(1) The person has special duties over the minor, has a common family life relationship with the minor, is a state functionary, or impersonates a state functionary, and commits the crime of rape or indecency;
(2) The person enters the minor's residence or student dormitory to commit the crime of rape or indecency;
(3) The person uses violent, coercive, anesthetic, or other forceful means to commit the crime of raping a girl under the age of 14 or molesting a child;
(4) The person commits the crime of rape or indecency against a child under the age of 12, a rural left-behind child, a minor with severe disability, or a minor with mental or intellectual developmental delay;
(5) The person molests multiple minors, or commits the crime of rape or indecency multiple times;
(6) The person causes consequences such as minor injury, pregnancy, or infection with a sexually transmitted disease to the minor victim;
(7) The person has a prior record of crimes of rape or indecency.
26. Where organizing, forcing, luring, harboring, or introducing a minor into prostitution constitutes a crime, a heavier punishment shall be imposed. Forcing a girl under the age of 14 into prostitution or luring a girl under the age of 14 into prostitution shall be convicted and punished in accordance with item (2) of paragraph 1 of Article 358 and paragraph 2 of Article 359 of the Criminal Law, respectively.
Where a person with special duties over a minor, a person with a common family life relationship with the minor, or a state functionary commits a crime of sexual assault such as organizing, forcing, luring, harboring, or introducing a minor into prostitution, the person shall be subject to severe punishment according to law.
27. Where a person who has reached the age of 14 but not the age of 16 occasionally has sexual relations with a girl under the age of 14, if the circumstances are minor and no serious consequences are caused, the act shall not be deemed a crime.

IV. Other Matters
28. When imposing a penalty on an adult criminal who has raped a minor, probation shall generally not be applied.
When determining whether to apply probation to a criminal who has committed sexual assault against a minor, the People's Court or the People's Procuratorate may entrust the community correction institution at the place where the criminal resides to investigate whether the probation would have a significant adverse impact on the community where the criminal resides. The entrusted community correction institution shall promptly organize an investigation and submit the investigation and assessment opinion to the entrusting organ within the prescribed time limit.
Where a penalty is imposed and probation is also declared, a restraining order may be declared at the same time based on the circumstances of the crime, prohibiting the criminal from engaging in work or activities related to minors during the probation period, and prohibiting the criminal from entering primary and secondary school campuses, kindergarten campuses, and other places where minors gather, except where it is necessary for the criminal's own schooling, residence, or other reasons, and approved by the enforcement organ.
29. Where a foreigner commits a crime such as raping or molesting a minor within the territory of China, the foreigner shall be punished according to law, and when imposing a penalty, deportation may be imposed independently or as a supplementary punishment. For acts that do not constitute a crime but constitute a violation of public security administration, or where the foreigner is not suitable to continue staying or residing in China due to committing a crime of sexual assault against a minor, the public security organ may, according to law, impose a time-limited departure or deportation.
30. For cases of rape or molestation of minors where the judgment has taken effect, the People's Court may publish the relevant judgment documents on the Internet under the premise of protecting the victim's privacy according to law, except where the minor is the offender.
31. For personal injury caused to a minor due to sexual assault, the minor victim and his or her legal representative or close relative may claim compensation for reasonable expenses such as medical expenses, nursing expenses, transportation expenses, and lost work expenses incurred for rehabilitation treatment. The People's Court shall support such claims according to law.
32. Where a minor suffers personal injury due to sexual assault while studying or living in a kindergarten, school, or other educational institution, and the victim and his or her legal representative or close relative files a lawsuit with the People's Court requesting the said unit to bear compensation liability, the People's Court shall support such claims according to law.
33. Where a minor is sexually assaulted by his or her guardian, other persons with guardianship qualifications, the civil affairs department, and other relevant entities and organizations may file an application with the People's Court to revoke the guardian's qualifications and appoint another guardian. The People's Court shall support such applications according to law.
34. Where a minor victim suffers personal injury due to a crime of sexual assault and is unable to obtain effective compensation in a timely manner, resulting in financial difficulties, the People's Courts, People's Procuratorates, and public security organs at all levels may, in conjunction with relevant departments, give priority consideration to granting judicial aid.
